newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: HK Bank executive says confidence in HK growing.
newsitem.headline: HK Bank executive says confidence in HK growing.

text.p: Confidence among the people of Hong Kong appears to have grown since the July 1 handover to China, a senior executive with the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp said on Tuesday.
Andrew Dixon, general manager, international, for the unit of HSBC Holdings told Reuters it appeared Hong Kong's residents had taken on a new lease of life.
"It's difficult to describe it. Everyone expected something dreadful to happen and of course it hasn't," Dixon said in an interview.
Dixon said the bank, one of the three bank note issuers in the former British colony, had been confident about Hong Kong's prospects, post-handover.
"What has surprised me personally, and a few other observers, either since the handover or during the handover, is the change in the people," Dixon said.
"Now that they are in charge of their own destiny, I think there is a huge confidence beginning to grow.
"I think they believe the one country, two-systems philosophy is going to work and as long as the people in Hong Kong believe something, it tends to happen," he said.
Dixon was in New Zealand to address an investment seminar organised by the British consulate in Auckland.
